name: autoclave-cycle-gauge
title: Autoclave Cycle Gauge
description: A card-scale status widget modelled on a steam sterilizer's combined pressure/temperature gauge: a needle sweeps a slow come-up ramp, sits through a timed hold with regulator chatter, then drops fast through an exhaust vent, while a temperature trace scrolls beneath it — three phases told apart by needle speed alone, never a printed number.
useWhen: a status/feedback moment standing in for a generic progress bar on a long-running background process, where the process genuinely has three visually distinct phases (a ramp, a hold, a fast release) and the shape of that profile is worth showing at a glance. Reach for progress-wick or progress-hatch instead for a single monotonic completion fraction with no distinct phase shapes; reach for meter-quota-meniscus instead when the value being shown is a static level/quota rather than a repeating three-phase cycle.
instruction: Build <AutoclaveCycleGauge label? className?> as a self-contained 2D canvas widget inside a bordered card (rounded-md border border-border bg-surface, fixed 4:3 canvas aspect-ratio, geometry derived entirely from the container's smaller dimension so it rescales cleanly at card size). Default label is a product-domain string ("In progress"), not the mechanic's name — callers slot in their own copy ("Rendering export", "Backing up", etc.) so the widget reads as a status moment on a real product surface, never as the sterilizer it's modelled on. It renders a circular dial occupying the card's upper ~68% and a horizontal scrolling temperature-trace strip in the lower band. CYCLE: a fixed unbounded 32s loop with three phases driven purely by elapsed real time (performance.now()-based, modulo 32s) — a 12s come-up ramp (0 to 15psi), a 15s hold sustained at 15psi with continuous +/-0.5deg needle tremor at 1.7Hz (regulator chatter, not synced to any phase boundary, floored to a minimum ~1.6px of needle-tip travel so it stays perceptible on small cards rather than going sub-pixel), then a 5s vent dropping 15psi back to 0, deliberately faster than the ramp so the three phases read apart from needle SPEED alone within the first 5 seconds, with no numeral or label ever printed. The needle sweeps a fixed 270deg arc (-135deg to +135deg from straight up) over a 0-20psi scale — the real 15psi setpoint never pins the needle at full deflection, so the same arc geometry always has visible headroom. DIAL RENDERING: a faint outer rim arc at 0.12 alpha and five minor tick marks at 0.28 alpha (0/25/50/75/100% of the scale) — no numerals, no bezel, no printed units, deliberately minimal so the widget reads as an ambient product-surface status moment rather than an instrument-panel readout. The needle itself is full-alpha var(--foreground) with a 1.5px stroke-width floor (so it survives against a light-theme dial face) and a small filled center hub. TEMPERATURE TRACE: a baseline stroke at 0.15 alpha plus a scrolling ridge built from a rolling sample history (one sample pushed per animation frame, oldest samples dropped once scrolled fully past the strip's left edge at 8px/s), rendered as a translucent (0.14 alpha) var(--foreground) fill under a 0.65 alpha stroke line — newest sample pinned to the strip's right edge, so the ridge visibly lengthens over the come-up phase (a viewer sees a longer ridge at t=5s than at t=2.5s even before the needle's ramp completes). TOKENS: every stroke/fill reads var(--foreground) or var(--background) exclusively, resolved once via getComputedStyle(document.documentElement) with no literal fallback of any kind; the mount routine retries on the next rAF until both --foreground and --background resolve and paints nothing before that; re-reads on every documentElement class-attribute mutation via a MutationObserver, and a ResizeObserver keeps canvas pixel dimensions and DPR in sync. No --ns-accent anywhere — this is a resting, non-interactive status surface, not a control. REDUCED MOTION: freezes at the hold-phase midpoint (cycle t=18s) — needle parked at exactly 15psi with tremor forced to zero (not merely evaluated at a near-neutral point in the tremor cycle), trace strip showing the full come-up ramp plus a partial flat hold segment, the single frame that shows all three phase shapes in outline (ramp slope, flat hold, and the strip stops before any vent segment exists) without ever starting an rAF loop. An IntersectionObserver pauses the rAF loop when the card scrolls off-screen and re-arms it (re-checking tokens for a theme flip that happened while hidden) on re-entry. Cleanup on unmount cancels every pending rAF and disconnects all three observers. No pointer interaction, no hover readout — the spec explicitly keeps this to needle motion alone as the one followable thing.
